# Prevention of neonatal Group B streptococcal infections

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Neonatology > Prevention of neonatal Group B streptococcal infections*

[Original Article Link](/library/xE0EB3)

---

## Summary

Group B <u>streptococcus</u> (<u>GBS</u>) infections are caused by <u>Streptococcus agalactiae</u> and are the leading cause of <u>neonatal sepsis</u>. <u>Early-onset GBS infection</u> occurs within the first 6 days of life and is typically due to <u>vertical transmission</u>. <u>Late-onset GBS infection</u> occurs between 7 and 89 days of life and is more commonly due to <u>horizontal transmission</u>. Prevention methods target both the pregnant individual and the <u>newborn</u>. Universal <u>prenatal GBS screening</u> and targeted <u>intrapartum</u> <u>GBS prophylaxis</u> have decreased <u>vertical transmission</u> and significantly reduced rates of <u>early-onset GBS infections</u>. In addition, all <u>newborns</u> undergo a <u>neonatal GBS risk assessment</u> shortly after <u>birth</u> to identify individuals who would benefit from early interventions (e.g., close observation, diagnostic evaluation, and/or <u>empiric antibiotics</u>) for <u>early-onset GBS infection</u>.

---

## Overview

### Classification of <u>GBS</u> infection in <u>infants</u> [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)[[4]](/library/9rdNjr0)




* Early-onset GBS infection

* Confirmed <u>S. agalactiae</u> infection that occurs between <u>birth</u> and 6 days of life  [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* Typically acquired vertically from the birthing parent during <u>labor</u> or delivery

* Includes <u>neonatal sepsis</u>, <u>neonatal meningitis</u>, and <u>neonatal pneumonia</u> [[5]](/library/Bedza60)

* Late-onset GBS infection

* Confirmed <u>S. agalactiae</u> infection that occurs between 7 and 89 days of life [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)

* Typically acquired horizontally from <u>nosocomial</u> or community environments

* Includes <u>bacteremia</u>, <u>neonatal meningitis</u>, <u>neonatal pneumonia</u>, <u>skin and soft tissue infections</u>, <u>osteomyelitis</u>, and <u>septic arthritis</u> [[5]](/library/Bedza60)

* Very <u>late-onset GBS infection</u>

* Confirmed <u>S. agalactiae</u> infection that occurs after ≥ 90 days of life [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)

* Primarily occurs in <u>infants</u> born very preterm or with <u>immunodeficiency</u>





> [!TIP]
> The cutoff used to define <u>early-onset GBS infection</u> (i.e., < 7 days) differs from the cutoff most commonly used to define <u>early-onset neonatal sepsis</u> (i.e., < 72 hours). [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[6]](/library/XLW9wN0)




### Risk factors for early-onset GBS infection [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)[[6]](/library/XLW9wN0)




* Maternal <u>GBS</u> <u>colonization</u> (e.g., high rectovaginal counts, <u>bacteriuria</u>)

* Maternal <u>intrapartum</u> temperature â¥ 38.0Â°C (â¥ 100.4Â°F) [[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* <u>Intra-amniotic infection</u>

* <u>Prolonged rupture of membranes</u> lasting ≥ 18 hours

* Previous <u>newborn</u> affected with <u>GBS</u>

* <u>Preterm birth</u>

* <u>Very low birth weight</u>





> [!TIP]
> Maternal <u>colonization</u> with <u>GBS</u> is the most significant <u>risk factor</u> for <u>early-onset neonatal GBS infections</u>. [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)




### Approach to prevention of <u>GBS</u> infection in <u>infants</u> [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)[[6]](/library/XLW9wN0)




* Perform universal <u>prenatal GBS screening</u>.

* Administer <u>intrapartum</u> <u>GBS prophylaxis</u> in pregnant individuals with indications.

* Perform a standardized assessment of all <u>newborns</u> for <u>GBS</u> <u>risk factors</u> to identify indications for further diagnostic testing and/or <u>antibiotic</u> treatment. [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)





> [!TIP]
> There is no proven prevention strategy for <u>late-onset GBS infection</u>. [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[6]](/library/XLW9wN0)

## Intrapartum prophylactic antibiotics for GBS

This section focuses on preventive measures for neonatal <u>GBS</u> infection administered to asymptomatic pregnant individuals during the <u>intrapartum</u> period. For management of <u>GBS</u>-related maternal infections, see “<u>Chorioamnionitis</u>,” “<u>Endometritis</u>,” “<u>Postpartum endometritis</u>,” “<u>Urinary tract infection in pregnancy</u>,” and “<u>Postpartum mastitis</u>.”




### Indications [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)[[7]](/library/wC1h8Q0)




<u>GBS prophylaxis</u> is indicated at the onset of <u>labor</u> and/or <u>rupture of membranes</u> in pregnant individuals with any of the following:




* History of <u>early-onset GBS infection</u> in a previous <u>newborn</u>

* Confirmed <u>GBS</u> <u>colonization</u> during the current <u>pregnancy</u>, i.e.:

* Positive <u>GBS</u> culture

* <u>GBS</u> <u>bacteriuria</u> (regardless of colony count)

* Unknown <u>GBS</u> culture result in the current <u>pregnancy</u> and any of the following: [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* Imminent <u>preterm delivery</u> < 37+0 weeks' <u>gestation</u> or <u>PPROM</u>

* <u>Prolonged rupture of membranes</u> lasting  ≥ 18 hours

* Maternal <u>intrapartum</u> temperature â¥ 38.0Â°C (â¥ 100.4Â°F)

* Positive <u>intrapartum</u> <u>GBS</u> <u>NAAT</u>

* Positive <u>GBS</u> culture or <u>GBS</u> <u>bacteriuria</u> in a previous <u>pregnancy</u>  [[3]](/library/1V12tf0)





> [!TIP]
> Regardless of <u>GBS</u> culture results, <u>intrapartum</u> <u>GBS prophylaxis</u> is not needed if <u>cesarean delivery</u> is performed before the onset of <u>labor</u> and membranes remain intact. [[3]](/library/1V12tf0)




### <u>Antibiotic</u> regimens [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)




If indicated, start <u>antibiotic prophylaxis</u> ideally ≥ 4 hours before delivery.




* No <u>penicillin</u> <u>allergy</u>: Start one of the following IV <u>beta-lactam antibiotics</u>. 

* Preferred: <u>penicillin G</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* Alternative: <u>ampicillin</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* <u>Penicillin</u> <u>allergy</u>

* <u>Low risk penicillin allergy</u>: <u>cefazolin</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* <u>Severe penicillin allergy</u>

* <u>Clindamycin</u>-susceptible <u>GBS</u>: <u>clindamycin</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)

* <u>Clindamycin</u>-resistant <u>GBS</u> or unknown <u>clindamycin</u> susceptibility: <u>vancomycin</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)





> [!WARNING]
> Do not delay any necessary obstetric interventions just to administer ≥ 4 hours of <u>GBS prophylaxis</u>. [[3]](/library/1V12tf0)




> [!TIP]
> If the severity of <u>penicillin</u> <u>allergy</u> is unclear, consider <u>penicillin</u> <u>allergy testing</u> during <u>pregnancy</u> to guide <u>GBS prophylaxis</u> at delivery. [[2]](/library/SiXyIB)[[3]](/library/1V12tf0)




### GBS prophylaxis considerations in preterm labor [[3]](/library/1V12tf0)




* Manage patients in consultation with an <u>obstetrician</u>.

* Start <u>intrapartum prophylactic antibiotics for GBS</u>.

* If <u>GBS</u> status is unknown, obtain <u>GBS</u> culture and <u>NAAT</u> prior to starting <u>antibiotics</u>.

* If <u>preterm labor</u> is arrested, <u>GBS prophylaxis</u> may be discontinued.

* If previously arrested <u>preterm labor</u> resumes:

* Review prior <u>GBS</u> culture results to determine if there are indications for <u>GBS prophylaxis</u>.

* For negative <u>GBS</u> culture results, repeat <u>GBS</u> <u>NAAT</u> and culture if ≥ 5 weeks since the prior result.
